common_name: Fortin's Giant Lily of the Valley (Large-Flowered Large-Leaved Convallaria)

planting.note: Plant pips (rhizome divisions) shallowly in fall or early spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial to full shade; Fortin's Giant is a larger-scaled selection with broader leaves and bigger flowers than the straight species.

directions: Plant pips shallowly in fall or early spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial to full shade. Fortin's Giant is a robust selection of lily of the valley bred for noticeably larger, broader leaves and bigger, more substantial white bells than the common species, giving a bolder textural presence in a woodland groundcover planting while retaining the same intensely sweet fragrance the plant is famous for. It spreads by underground rhizomes to form dense colonies over time and goes summer-dormant as conditions warm, reemerging reliably each spring. It thrives in cool, moist, shaded sites and can be aggressive in ideal conditions, so plant where it can naturalize freely or contain the spread with buried edging. All parts of the plant are highly toxic if ingested, so site it away from areas where children or pets might sample the berries or foliage.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Plants Database
